description:
The Total Health Check-up Scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India under the aegis of the Goa Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (GBOCWWB).

This scheme was officially launched on 1st January 2020.

The primary objective of the Total Health Check-up Scheme is to provide comprehensive health check-ups for construction workers in Goa.

The scheme aims to ensure that construction workers receive regular health assessments to identify potential health issues early.

The target population for this scheme includes all registered construction workers in Goa.

As of October 2023, there are approximately 30,000 registered construction workers in Goa.

The scheme is designed to cover various health parameters including blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol levels, and body mass index.

Workers will also receive screenings for common diseases such as tuberculosis and hepatitis.

The Total Health Check-up Scheme provides free health check-ups to eligible construction workers.

Each worker is entitled to a comprehensive health check-up once a year.

The monetary value of each health check-up is estimated to be around INR 1,500.

This amount covers various tests and consultations with healthcare professionals.

The eligibility criteria for the Total Health Check-up Scheme include being a registered construction worker under the GBOCWWB.

Workers must be at least 18 years of age to qualify for the scheme.

There is no upper age limit for eligibility.

Additionally, workers must have a valid registration with the Goa Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

To apply for the Total Health Check-up Scheme, workers must follow a specific process.

First, they need to visit the official GBOCWWB website or the nearest GBOCWWB office.

They must fill out an application form which is available online or at the office.

The application form requires personal details such as name, age, registration number, and contact information.

Workers must also provide proof of their registration with the GBOCWWB.

This can be done by submitting a copy of their registration certificate.

Once the application is completed, it must be submitted to the GBOCWWB office.

After submission, the GBOCWWB will verify the application and registration details.

Upon successful verification, workers will receive a health check-up appointment.

The health check-ups are conducted at designated healthcare facilities across Goa.

These facilities are equipped to perform the necessary tests and consultations.

The frequency of health check-ups under this scheme is once a year for each registered worker.

The health check-up schedule is typically organized in the first quarter of each calendar year.

Workers are notified of their appointment dates via SMS or phone calls.

The implementing authority for the Total Health Check-up Scheme is the Goa Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment, Government of Goa.

For any inquiries or assistance, workers can contact the GBOCWWB office directly.

The contact number for the GBOCWWB office is +91 832 241 6000.

The email address for inquiries is gbocewb@gmail.com.

The Total Health Check-up Scheme is part of a broader initiative to improve the health and well-being of construction workers in Goa.

Construction workers often face health risks due to the nature of their work.

The scheme aims to mitigate these risks through regular health monitoring.

By providing free health check-ups, the government seeks to promote preventive healthcare among workers.

The scheme also aligns with the national goals of improving healthcare access and outcomes for vulnerable populations.

The Total Health Check-up Scheme is expected to reduce the incidence of occupational diseases among construction workers.

Regular health assessments can lead to early detection and treatment of health issues.

This proactive approach is crucial in ensuring the long-term health of workers.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of health education among construction workers.

Workers are encouraged to adopt healthier lifestyles based on the findings of their health check-ups.

The GBOCWWB collaborates with various healthcare providers to ensure quality services under this scheme.

The initiative has received positive feedback from workers who have benefited from the health check-ups.

The Total Health Check-up Scheme is a significant step towards ensuring the welfare of construction workers in Goa.

It reflects the government's commitment to enhancing the quality of life for this workforce.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare measures for construction workers in India.

Overall, the Total Health Check-up Scheme is a vital initiative aimed at safeguarding the health of construction workers in Goa.

It provides them with the necessary resources to maintain their health and well-being.

The scheme is a testament to the government's recognition of the challenges faced by construction workers.

By facilitating access to healthcare, the scheme aims to empower workers and improve their quality of life.

In summary, the Total Health Check-up Scheme is a comprehensive health initiative for construction workers in Goa.

It offers free annual health check-ups and aims to promote preventive healthcare.

The scheme is accessible to all registered construction workers aged 18 and above.

The application process is straightforward and requires proof of registration.

The GBOCWWB oversees the implementation of the scheme and ensures quality healthcare services.

This initiative is crucial for the health and welfare of construction workers in the state.
